2026 NFB Austin Restaurant Guide presented by TJO Presents

Compiled by TJ of TJO Presents, independent event curator, accessibility consultant, and hospitality professional.

Restaurants, bars, cafés, coffee shops, bakeries, and entertainment venues are organized by walking time from the JW Marriott Austin rather than alphabetically, making it easy to find the closest options first.

Worth the Uber

While we're fortunate to have quite a few places within easy walking distance from the convention hotel, there are certainly places worth the Uber or transit journey. From a combination of friends and trusted sources, I'm providing some of those below.

Papercut + Konbini

908 E 5th Street, Austin, TX.

0.9 miles; about a 4 minute drive.

This cocktail bar is also home to a highly innovative late-night sushi pop-up combining Japanese technique with Texan and coastal Mexican flavors.

$$-$$$

Casino El Camino

517 E 6th Street, Austin, TX.

0.6 miles; about a 3 minute drive.

Beloved, well-priced burger spot.

$-$$

Amy’s Ice Creams

1012 W 6th Street, Austin, TX.

An Austin institution for more than 40 years, Amy’s has hundreds of flavors of thick, creamy ice cream across the area, with milkshakes, ices, freshly baked waffle cones, and hot fudge sundaes; Mexican Vanilla is the must-try.

$-$$

Texas Chili Parlor

1409 Lavaca Street, Austin, TX.

0.9 miles; about a 5 minute drive.

Hole-in-the-wall Tex-Mex chili joint serving classic Texas chili and margaritas.

$-$$

Franklin Barbecue

900 E 11th Street, Austin, TX.

1.2 miles; about a 6 minute drive.

World-class barbecue served by the pound or in sandwiches from an outdoor counter, with notoriously long lines; service starts at 11 AM and runs until sold out, no later than 3 PM, with limited outdoor seating available.

$$$

Better Half Coffee & Cocktails

406 Walsh Street, Austin, TX.

1.4 miles; about a 9 minute drive.

Another Eater Austin best-restaurant pick, praised for great coffee and a first-rate lineup of beer, wine, and cocktails, serving well-priced, creative breakfast, lunch, and dinner with equal love paid to the coffee and cocktail programs.

$$

La Barbecue

2401 E Cesar Chavez Street, Austin, TX.

1.7 miles; about a 6 minute drive.

An Eater must-eat in Austin and Michelin-starred counter-style barbecue spot with slightly more innovative combinations on the menu; expect classic barbecue vibes indoors or on the patio, and be prepared to wait at least an hour unless you order ahead.

$$-$$$

801 Red River Street, Austin, TX.

Restaurant-style barbecue at very reasonable prices, famous for sauces and marinades; they also have a live music venue, but only seem to have gospel brunch on Sunday during the convention dates.

$$-$$$

Nixta Taqueria

2512 E 12th Street, Austin, TX.

2.8 miles; about a 9 minute drive.

James Beard Award-winning and Michelin-recognized chef Edgar Rico has been called one of the country’s most lauded taco chefs, blending fine dining, Mexican-American cuisine, the on-site garden, and co-owner Sara Mardanbigi’s Iranian background.

$$-$$$

Accessible menu

Micklethwait Barbecue

4602 Tanney Street, Austin, TX.

4 miles; about a 15 minute drive.

Considered one of the best new-school Texas barbecue spots, this counter-service spot housed in a converted church serves classic Texas barbecue, but its sides game is a cut above many of the others; pork ribs are only available on weekends, and they are only open Thursday through Sunday.

$-$$

Chi'Lantro BBQ

1509 S Lamar Boulevard, Austin, TX.

2.3 miles; about an 11 minute drive.

Another recommendation from your brother, this bowl-centric rapidly expanding local chain serves Korean-style barbecue, loaded Kimchi Fries™, Korean wings, and more.

$-$$

Leroy and Lewis Barbecue

5621 Emerald Forest Drive, Austin, TX.

7 miles; about a 15 minute drive.

A bit more of a trek than everything else on this list, but your brother was incredibly insistent that this is the spot; what began as a food truck has evolved into a spacious storefront serving meats by the quarter pound, sandwiches, tacos, apps, and daily specials, with counter ordering for most barbecue items, bar ordering for the Any Time Eats section, a dedicated temperature-controlled dining room, and outdoor seating.

$$
